candidates.title: California Executive Order N-9-26 sets deadlines for independent verification rules and seeks recommendations on a frontier-model kill switch and loss-of-control incident reporting
candidates.summary: Governor Newsom signed Executive Order N-9-26 on 18 September 2026, effective immediately. It sets deadlines for the Government Operations Agency to complete the requirements of Government Code section 8898.1 and to develop and publicly post application requirements, procedures and criteria for independent verification organizations (by 1 May 2027), and to complete section 11549.82(a) and begin the actions required by 11549.82(b) (by 1 December 2027). It also directs the Government Operations Agency, in consultation with the Governor's Office of Emergency Services, to submit recommendations to the Governor's office by 16 November 2026, developed in consultation with national experts, on the technical feasibility and potential efficacy of amendments to existing state AI safety and security laws, covering at least: embedding independent verification organizations onsite at large frontier developers; independent verification of required safety frameworks, transparency reports and risk assessments; a 'kill switch' for frontier models whose efficacy is verified on an ongoing basis by an independent verification organization; and updating the definition of critical safety incidents to include a range of loss-of-control incidents. The order states that it does not create any rights or benefits enforceable at law or in equity; its directives are addressed to state agencies.
candidates.why_it_matters: The order does not change obligations for frontier developers today. It signals the content of possible amendments to California's existing AI safety and security laws and sets deadlines for the Government Operations Agency to implement Gov. Code 8898.1 and to complete and begin actions under Gov. Code 11549.82. The recommendations are due to the Governor by 16 November 2026.

candidates.title: Executive Order 14434 directs federal agencies to use 'Super Intelligence' in place of 'Artificial Intelligence'
candidates.summary: The White House page for Executive Order 14434, 'Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence', is dated 29 September 2026. It directs executive departments and agencies to use 'Super Intelligence' and 'SI' instead of 'Artificial Intelligence' and 'AI' in official correspondence, public communications, websites, reports, policy documents and other non-statutory documents, to the maximum extent permitted by law. Previously issued regulations, presidential actions, contracts, grants and historical documents need not be altered. The order defines the terms as the technologies and systems encompassed by the term 'artificial intelligence' as defined in 15 U.S.C. 9401(3). Within 60 days the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology is to submit to the President proposed legislative language for a federal definition of 'Super Intelligence' and 'SI', including an assessment of whether it should modify or supersede the existing statutory definition of 'artificial intelligence' and any conforming amendments to existing statutory references, as appropriate. The order does not address preemption of state law.
candidates.why_it_matters: The order changes federal agency terminology and starts a 60 day process toward a statutory definition. It sets no obligations for private parties on its face. Existing statutes and rules keep their current wording unless Congress or later action amends them.

candidates.title: California governor signs SB 1119 (Adam's Law) on companion chatbot child safety, as part of a 13-bill child online safety package
candidates.summary: On 10 September 2026 the governor's office announced the signing of 13 child online safety bills. Per the release, SB 1119 (Padilla, Wicks, Bauer-Kahan), 'Companion chatbots: children's safety', requires protections around companion chatbots for children, including crisis protocols in the case of suicidal ideation, parental controls and notifications should a child disable safety settings, plus independent child safety audits and annual risk assessments. Sen. Padilla's office, in a release stating the bill passed on 31 August 2026 (Senate 39-0, Assembly 64-4), calls the bill Adam's Law. Other bills in the package, by their official short titles, include AB 1709 ('Covered platforms: age restriction: e-Safety Advisory Commission'), SB 1276 ('Crimes: sexual exploitation of a child') and AB 1159 ('Student personal information'). The governor's release describes the package's provisions in unnumbered bullets; bill-by-bill attribution beyond SB 1119 was not verified. Chaptered texts, chapter numbers and operative dates were not checked.
candidates.why_it_matters: Companion chatbot operators serving California users should check the chaptered text for who is covered, audit timing and operative dates, which this item does not establish.

instrument_candidates.name: California SB 1119 (Adam's Law): companion chatbot child safety
instrument_candidates.summary: California statute signed 10 September 2026 setting child safety requirements for companion chatbot operators, including crisis protocols, parental controls and independent audits. Described from the governor's release and Sen. Padilla's release only; operative dates not verified.
key_obligations: Safety protocols including crisis protocols in the case of suicidal ideation
Parental controls and notifications when children disable safety features
Annual risk assessments and independent child safety audits (Padilla release: audit findings submitted to the Attorney General)
Incident reporting mechanism overseen by the Attorney General (per Padilla release)
Private right of action for families harmed by violations (per Padilla release)

timeline.note: Passed Senate 39-0 and Assembly 64-4 and sent to the Governor, per the author's office.
Governor announced signing of SB 1119 as part of a 13 bill child online safety package.
